name: Jotham
overview: Jotham was a male king from the tribe of Judah, noted for his faithful leadership as the son of King Uzziah (also known as Azariah). He did what was right in the sight of the LORD, following the example set by his father. His reign is marked by a commitment to righteousness despite the ongoing corruption among the people.
namesAndTitles: The name Jotham means 'YHWH will complete,' reflecting a divine assurance embedded in his identity. He also held the title 'King of Judah,' indicating his royal authority over the southern kingdom. Neither name was explicitly given by God but carries significant meaning within the biblical context.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Jotham as the son of Azariah (Uzziah) and infers that Jerusha was his mother and Ahaz his son. These relationships place him firmly within the Davidic royal lineage, underscoring his role in the continuity of Judah's monarchy.
scriptureSignificance: Jotham is significant as a king who maintained faithful leadership by doing what was right before the LORD, continuing the legacy of his father Uzziah. His reign demonstrates that godly leadership does not guarantee the repentance of the people, highlighting the limitations of human authority when hearts remain hardened. His construction projects and military victories reflect his active role in strengthening Judah, even as spiritual decline persisted among the nation.
